Amazon Bedrock calculates the price based on the AWS Region\\\\n from which you make the request (the source AWS Region).\\\\n* **Streamlined monitoring** \u2013 When using\\\\n global cross-Region inference, CloudWatch and CloudTrail continue to record log entries\\\\n in your source AWS Region, simplifying observability and management. Even\\\\n though your requests are processed across different AWS Regions worldwide,\\\\n you maintain a centralized view of your application\\'s performance and usage\\\\n patterns through your familiar AWS monitoring tools.\\\\n* **Worldwide request routing** \u2013 With global\\\\n cross-Region inference, your requests can be processed by compute across\\\\n supported commercial AWS Regions worldwide rather than within a single\\\\n geography\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/global-cross-region-inference.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Amazon Bedrock\",\"context\":\"#### Amazon Bedrock \u2014 Cross-Region Inference (CRIS)\\\\n\\\\n##### Overview\\\\n\\\\nCross-region inference (CRIS) profiles let Bedrock route requests across AWS Regions to improve throughput. You can verify model availability, applicable service quotas, and model-specific pricing through current AWS documentation and AWS pricing pages\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/building-a-self-service-llm-gateway-with-amazon-bedrock-and-litellm/\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Scale AI in South Africa using Amazon Bedrock global cross-Region inference with Anthropic\\xa0Claude\\xa04.5 models | Artificial Intelligence\",\"context\":\"## Understanding cross-Region inference\\\\n\\\\nCross-Region inference is a powerful feature that organizations can use to seamlessly distribute inference processing across multiple Regions. This capability helps you get higher throughput while building at scale, allowing your generative AI applications to remain responsive and reliable even under heavy load.\\\\n\\\\nAn inference profile in Amazon Bedrock defines a foundation model (FM) and one or more Regions to which it can route model invocation requests. Inference profiles operate on two key concepts:\\\\n\\\\n* **Source Region** \u2013 The Region from which the API request is made\\\\n* **Destination Region** \u2013 A Region to which Amazon Bedrock can route the request for inference\\\\n\\\\nCross-Region inference operates through the secure AWS network with end-to-end encryption for both data in transit and at rest. When a customer submits an inference request from a source Region, cross-Region inference intelligently routes the request to one of the destination Regions configured for the inference profile over the Amazon Bedrock managed network.\\\\n\\\\nThe key distinction is that while inference processing (the transient computation) can occur in another Region, data at rest\u2014including logs, knowledge bases, and stored configurations\u2014is designed to remain within your source Region. (Recommended for use-cases with data residency needs.)\\\\n2. **Global cross-Region inference**: Global cross-Region inference further enhances cross-Region inference by enabling the routing of inference requests to supported commercial Regions worldwide, optimizing available resources and enabling higher model throughput. (Recommended for use-cases that don\u2019t have data residency needs)\",\"url\":\"https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/scale-ai-in-south-africa-using-amazon-bedrock-global-cross-region-inference-with-anthropic-claude-4-5-models/\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"How do I restrict Amazon Bedrock cross-Region inference routing to specific Regions?\",\"context\":\"### Choose an inference profile type\\\\n\\\\nAmazon Bedrock offers [geographic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/geographic-cross-region-inference.html) and [global](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/global-cross-region-inference.html) cross-Region inference profiles. Certain models are available only in a single Region. Check\\xa0[Models at a glance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/model-cards.html) for the profiles a model supports. For SageMaker model discovery, customization, or endpoints, use aws-ai-ml.\\\\n\\\\nServices: bedrock, bedrock-runtime, bedrock-mantle, bedrock-agent, bedrock-agent-runtime, bedrock-agentcore-control, bedrock-agentcore\\\\nTasks: deploy, debug, optimize, design, migrate\\\\nPersona: developer, devops, architect\\\\nWorkload: generative-ai, rag, agents\",\"skill_name\":\"amazon-bedrock\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"caching-for-llm-inference\",\"skill_description\":\"Sets up a shared L2 KV cache for self-hosted LLM inference on Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey, so GPU servers load prefill KV state over EFA RDMA instead of recomputing it. {"id": "aa26e577-622d-4970-ac5f-6cfe57530905", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_7MRJ0pRLRSibMXVmvlr0iI", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"status\":\"SUCCESS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/global-cross-region-inference.html\",\"content\":\"Table of Contents:\\n- Global cross-Region inference (char 0-14123)\\n  - Benefits of global cross-Region inference (char 415-1466)\\n  - Global cross-Region inference considerations (char 1467-2090)\\n  - IAM policy requirements for global cross-Region inference (char 2091-6797)\\n    - Disable global cross-Region inference (char 5156-6797)\\n  - Service Control Policy requirements for Global cross-Region inference (char 6798-10631)\\n    - Disable global cross-Region inference (char 8998-9875)\\n    - AWS Control Tower implementation (char 9876-10631)\\n  - Request limit increases for global cross-Region inference (char 10632-12392)\\n  - Use Global cross-Region inference (char 12393-13277)\\n  - Implement global cross-Region inference (char 13278-14123)\\n\\n# Global cross-Region inference\\n\\nGlobal cross-Region inference extends cross-Region inference beyond geographic\\nboundaries, enabling the routing of inference requests to supported commercial\\nAWS Regions worldwide.\\n\\nGlobal cross-Region inference is available for the models that have a global\\ninference profile. For the list of supported models and Regions, see Supported Regions and models for inference profiles.\\n\\n## Benefits of global cross-Region inference\\n\\nWith global cross-Region inference, you get the following advantages over a\\ngeographic cross-Region inference profile:\\n\\n* **Cost-efficiency** \u2013 You save approximately\\n  10% on both input and output token pricing compared to geographic\\n  cross-Region inference. Amazon Bedrock calculates the price based on the AWS Region\\n  from which you make the request (the source AWS Region).\\n* **Streamlined monitoring** \u2013 When using\\n  global cross-Region inference, CloudWatch and CloudTrail continue to record log entries\\n  in your source AWS Region, simplifying observability and management. Even\\n  though your requests are processed across different AWS Regions worldwide,\\n  you maintain a centralized view of your application's performance and usage\\n  patterns through your familiar AWS monitoring tools.\\n* **Worldwide request routing** \u2013 With global\\n  cross-Region inference, your requests can be processed by compute across\\n  supported commercial AWS Regions worldwide rather than within a single\\n  geography.\\n\\n## Global cross-Region inference considerations\\n\\nNote the following information about Global cross-Region inference:\\n\\n* For default cross-Region throughput quotas when using Global\\n  inference profiles, see the **Global Cross-region\\n  model inference requests per minute for ${Model}** and\\n  **Global Cross-region model inference tokens per\\n  minute for ${Model}** values in Amazon Bedrock service\\n  quotas in the *AWS General\\n  Reference*.\\n\\n  You can request, view, and manage quotas for the Global Cross-Region\\n  Inference Profile from the Service Quotas console or by using AWS CLI commands in your\\n  **source region**.\\n\\n## IAM policy requirements for global cross-Region inference\\n\\nTo enable global cross-Region inference for your users, you must apply a\\nthree-part IAM policy to the role. The following is an example IAM policy to\\nprovide granular control. You can replace `<REQUESTING REGION>` in\\nthe example policy with the AWS Region you are operating in.\\n\\n```\\n{\\n    \\\"Version\\\": \\\"2012-10-17\\\",\\n    \\\"Statement\\\": [\\n        {\\n            \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"GrantGlobalCrisInferenceProfileRegionAccess\\\",\\n            \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Allow\\\",\\n            \\\"Action\\\": \\\"bedrock:InvokeModel\\\",\\n            \\\"Resource\\\": [\\n                \\\"arn:aws:bedrock:<REQUESTING REGION>:<ACCOUNT>:inference-profile/global.<MODEL NAME>\\\"\\n            ],\\n            \\\"Condition\\\": {\\n                \\\"StringEquals\\\": {\\n                    \\\"aws:RequestedRegion\\\": \\\"<REQUESTING REGION>\\\"\\n                }\\n            }\\n        },\\n        {\\n            \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"GrantGlobalCrisInferenceProfileInRegionModelAccess\\\",\\n            \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Allow\\\",\\n            \\\"Action\\\": \\\"bedrock:InvokeModel\\\",\\n            \\\"Resource\\\": [\\n                \\\"arn:aws:bedrock:<REQUESTING REGION>::foundation-model/<MODEL NAME>\\\"\\n            ],\\n            \\\"Condition\\\": {\\n                \\\"StringEquals\\\": {\\n                    \\\"aws:RequestedRegion\\\": \\\"<REQUESTING REGION>\\\",\\n                    \\\"bedrock:InferenceProfileArn\\\": \\\"arn:aws:bedrock:<REQUESTING REGION>:<ACCOUNT>:inference-profile/global.<MODEL NAME>\\\"\\n                }\\n            }\\n        },\\n        {\\n            \\\"Sid\\\": \\\"GrantGlobalCrisInferenceProfileGlobalModelAccess\\\",\\n            \\\"Effect\\\": \\\"Allow\\\",\\n            \\\"Action\\\": \\\"bedrock:InvokeModel\\\",\\n            \\\"Resource\\\": [\\n                \\\"[redacted ARN]<MODEL NAME>\\\"\\n            ],\\n            \\\"Condition\\\": {\\n                \\\"StringEquals\\\": {\\n                    \\\"aws:RequestedRegion\\\": \\\"unspecified\\\",\\n                    \\\"bedrock:InferenceProfileArn\\\": \\\"arn:aws:bedrock:<REQUESTING REGION>:<ACCOUNT>:inference-profile/global.<MODEL NAME>\\\"\\n                }\\n            }\\n        }\\n    ]\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThe first part of the policy grants access to the Regional inference profile in\\nyour requesting AWS Region. The second part provides access to the Regional FM\\nresource. The third part grants access to the global FM resource, which enables the\\ncross-Region routing capability.\\n\\nWhen implementing these policies, include all three resource Amazon Resource\\nNames (ARNs) in your IAM statements:\\n\\n* The Regional inference profile ARN follows the pattern\\n  `arn:aws:bedrock:REGION:ACCOUNT:inference-profile/global.MODEL-NAME`.\\n  Use this ARN to grant access to the global inference profile in the source\\n  AWS Region.\\n* The Regional FM uses\\n  `arn:aws:bedrock:REGION::foundation-model/MODEL-NAME`. Use\\n  this ARN to grant access to the FM in the source AWS Region.\\n* The global FM requires\\n  `[redacted ARN]`. Use this ARN\\n  to grant access to the FM in different global AWS Regions.\\n\\nThe global FM ARN has no AWS Region or account specified, which is intentional\\nand required for the cross-Region functionality.\\n\\n### Disable global cross-Region inference\\n\\nYou can choose from two primary approaches to implement deny policies to\\nglobal CRIS for specific IAM roles, each with different use cases and\\nimplications:\\n\\n* **Remove an IAM policy** \u2013 The first\\n  method involves removing one or more of the three required IAM\\n  policies from user permissions. Because global CRIS requires all three\\n  policies to function, removing a policy will result in denied\\n  access.\\n* **Implement a deny policy** \u2013 The second\\n  approach is to implement an explicit deny policy that specifically\\n  targets global CRIS inference profiles. This method provides clear\\n  documentation of your security intent and makes sure that even if\\n  someone accidentally adds the required allow policies later, the\\n  explicit deny will take precedence.
